title: One Base Moves the Reading Frame

scenes.tts: Change one base in a gene, and the protein may not change at all. Add one base, and every amino acid after it can change. Both facts follow from one rule. The cell reads a message of four bases, called messenger R N A.
scenes.caption: Change one base in a gene, and the protein may not change at all. Add one base, and every amino acid after it can change. Both facts follow from one rule. The cell reads a message of four bases, called messenger RNA.
scenes.visual: An mRNA letter strip; one letter flips, then one letter is inserted; the protein stays a question mark.
scenes.narration: Change one base in a gene, and the protein may not change at all. Add one base, and every amino acid after it can change. Both facts follow from one rule. The cell reads a message of four bases, called messenger RNA.

scenes.tts: Pairs of bases give only sixteen words, too few for twenty amino acids. Triplets give sixty-four, more than enough. A codon is a group of three bases that specifies one amino acid or a stop. Of the sixty-four, sixty-one stand for amino acids and three mean stop. Reading usually starts at the first A U G, and runs on in groups of three.
scenes.caption: Pairs of bases give only sixteen words, too few for twenty amino acids. Triplets give sixty-four, more than enough. Reading usually starts at the first AUG, and runs on in groups of three.
scenes.visual: Dot grids of 16 and 64 words, then the mRNA strip with AUG marked and triplet boxes laid out from it.

scenes.tts: Each codon is looked up in the genetic code. A U G is methionine, G C U is alanine, and U G G is tryptophan. A A A is lysine, C C U is proline, and G A C is aspartate. Then U A G is a stop, and it adds no amino acid. The chain is six residues long.
scenes.caption: Each codon is looked up in the genetic code. AUG is methionine, GCU is alanine, and UGG is tryptophan. AAA is lysine, CCU is proline, and GAC is aspartate. Then UAG is a stop, and it adds no amino acid. The chain is six residues long.
scenes.visual: Each codon box gets its amino acid chip below it; the stop box turns red and the six-residue chain is bracketed.
scenes.narration: Each codon is looked up in the genetic code. AUG is methionine, GCU is alanine, and UGG is tryptophan. AAA is lysine, CCU is proline, and GAC is aspartate. Then UAG is a stop, and it adds no amino acid. The chain is six residues long.

scenes.tts: Now change one base. First, G C U to G C C still means alanine, so the change is silent. Second, G C U to A C U means threonine, so one amino acid swaps, a missense change. Third, U G G to U G A is a stop, so the chain ends after two residues, a nonsense change.
scenes.caption: Now change one base. First, GCU to GCC still means alanine, so the change is silent. Second, GCU to ACU means threonine, so one amino acid swaps, a missense change. Third, UGG to UGA is a stop, so the chain ends after two residues, a nonsense change.
scenes.visual: Three cases on the strip, each reset to a question mark first: silent keeps Ala, missense gives Thr, nonsense ends the chain after Ala.
scenes.narration: Now change one base. First, GCU to GCC still means alanine, so the change is silent. Second, GCU to ACU means threonine, so one amino acid swaps, a missense change. Third, UGG to UGA is a stop, so the chain ends after two residues, a nonsense change.

scenes.tts: Now add one base, a G, right after the start codon. The start codon stays. Every base after the new G slides along by one place. The triplets regroup, and the protein becomes methionine, glycine, leucine, glutamate, threonine. Then a stop that was out of frame now comes early, and the protein is shorter.

scenes.visual: A yellow G drops in after AUG; letters slide one slot under fixed triplet boxes; chips reset to question marks and become Met-Gly-Leu-Glu-Thr, stop; the old chain stays faint below.

scenes.tts: Crick and colleagues studied this in phage T 4, and called the two kinds of mutation plus and minus. Picture its gene as a sentence of three-letter words. A plus with a nearby minus often restored function. Two pluses did not, but three pluses restored wild or nearly wild growth in the combinations they tested. Keep this rule: one base more or less moves the frame, and the frame sets every codon.
